set.body:
Context

This is the external dependency gate for reframe4s MIG-210 / AC-006. reframe4s currently pins Ravel 473c33bb1e53ec83256935861639581b92d3fbcd, which does not provide the kernel facilities needed for production resampling. The current dirty Ravel tree appears to contain candidate implementations in NDArray.scala, Layout.scala, MutableNDArray.scala, ArrayBuilder.scala, ScalarIndexingSuite, and PhaseBSuite. The request is to stabilize and prove those facilities, not invent a competing array layer in reframe4s.

Required public contract

1. NDArray fixed-arity reads for ranks 1 through 4, sufficient for the accepted Rank3 and Rank4 resampling kernels. Steady-state reads must not allocate per element. Indexing must remain correct for contiguous arrays and offset, sliced, negative-stride, permuted, and broadcast views, with explicit rank and bounds failures.
2. A consuming immutable-output construction API, currently shaped as NDArray.build(shape)(ArrayBuilder => Unit) or an equivalent public contract. It must allocate one destination storage, permit allocation-free linear writes, return an immutable NDArray backed by that same destination without an output-sized copy, and make the builder unusable after the callback returns. If the callback fails, no partially built NDArray may be published.
3. The contract must be available from the public ravel-core artifact on JVM and Scala.js. reframe4s must not need private Ravel APIs, reflection, borrowed mutable output, or its own duplicate storage/indexing kernel.

Acceptance evidence

- Commit correctness tests for rank-1 through rank-4 scalar indexing, including every view class above, negative indices where supported, arity mismatch, bounds failures, and mutable-view write locality.
- Commit builder tests covering ordered and non-ordered writes as supported, bounds failures, post-callback sealing, callback failure, zero-length output, and representative primitive DTypes.
- Add a JVM allocation benchmark or profiler-backed test whose hot loop consumes a checksum so it cannot be eliminated. After input/setup allocation is excluded, fixed-rank traversal must show no allocation proportional to element count.
- Add a builder allocation and peak-memory benchmark. Allocation may scale as one primitive destination buffer plus O(1); it must show no per-element allocation, no materialized coordinate collection, and no second output-sized buffer/copy. Include at least Rank3 input reads with a Rank3 output and Rank4 reads with linear output writes.
- Verify the implementation with the normal JVM test suite and optimized Scala.js linking/tests. Record commands and results in the issue notes.
- From a clean external sbt consumer using only published public APIs, compile and run a small Rank3/Rank4 kernel probe against the candidate revision.
- Document the supported rank range, indexing failure semantics, builder lifetime/ownership, exception behavior, and thread-safety boundary.
- Land all required source, test, benchmark, and documentation changes; obtain green CI; push an immutable commit. Record the exact commit SHA and dependency coordinates so reframe4s can update its pin and run AC-006.

Non-goals

- Interpolation, pull-map polarity, transform compilation, workspaces, or medical-image semantics in Ravel.
- General NumPy performance parity or arbitrary-rank scalar syntax beyond the Rank1-4 consumer gate.
- Exposing mutable storage after construction or requiring reframe4s to depend on Ravel internals.

Done means reframe4s can replace pin 473c33bb1e53ec83256935861639581b92d3fbcd with the recorded green SHA and pass an external capability probe without duplicating Ravel.
set.title: Stabilize and release allocation-free kernel APIs required by reframe4s
